title: A Royal Guard for a Chess Book
body: Back in the sixteenth century, writing a chess book was a very big deal. The King of Spain himself signed a special decree to protect Ruy López's new chess guide. Anyone who dared to copy or disobey this royal order faced a massive fine of twenty thousand coins, which would be worth a fortune today.

variants.lucy: Hundreds of years ago, a thoughtful player named Ruy López wrote a special guide filled with chess secrets. The King of Spain wanted to protect these precious pages, so he signed a royal paper just for this book. This gentle guard of ink made sure that no one could copy the writer's hard work without permission.
variants.luca: Imagine having the King of Spain protect your chess strategies! He made a strict royal rule that absolutely nobody could copy Ruy's new book. Anyone who dared to break this law faced a giant penalty of twenty thousand coins. That would be worth a massive fortune today!

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath
